notes: Rendering journeys. A scripted model is what makes these possible: the response bytes are fixed, so the rendered frame can be asserted exactly. Assertions favour negative checks -- markdown syntax that must NOT survive to the screen -- because a renderer leaking its own markup is the failure users actually see. Tokens asserted absent are chosen so they never exist even transiently mid-stream. Parsing semantics are already covered by unit tests under src/utils/__tests__; these cover the seam those cannot reach: a real ACP stream, real store batching, and a real 120-column terminal.

scenarios.name: Every markdown block type reaches the screen
scenarios.description: One response carrying a heading, inline emphasis, nested and ordered lists, a blockquote and a rule -- asserts the content renders and the markdown syntax does not survive
scenarios.observe: Heading renders bold with no leading '#'. Emphasis markers are consumed, not printed. Bullets keep their '- ' prefix, the nested bullet is indented under its parent, and the ordered item keeps its number. The blockquote renders behind a vertical bar with its '>' consumed, and the rule renders as a divider. The stripped '#' and '>' markers are what distinguish real rendering from raw markdown passed straight through -- list prefixes alone cannot, since they are identical in source and output.

scenarios.name: Fenced code block renders without its fence
scenarios.description: A fenced block arriving in one piece renders every code line and drops the fence markers
scenarios.observe: All three code lines render with relative indentation preserved. No fence markers appear, and no language label is drawn -- the language only drives highlighting, which is why 'python' must not appear anywhere on screen. Highlight colours themselves are not asserted: the screen snapshot carries no style attributes.

scenarios.name: Inline markers split across stream chunks still resolve
scenarios.description: Bold and inline-code markers are delivered straddling chunk boundaries, paced past the render batch window -- the settled frame must show resolved formatting, not raw markers
scenarios.observe: Each marker pair is split across two scripted events, so no single delta contains a complete pair. What is gated is final assembly: the settled frame shows styled text with no stray asterisks or backticks, meaning the incremental parser either handled the delta or fell back to a reparse. What is NOT gated is the transient display -- predicates run only after the turn goes idle, so a raw marker flashing mid-stream would not fail this scenario.

scenarios.name: Long paragraph wraps without losing either end
scenarios.description: A single logical line far wider than the terminal must wrap rather than truncate -- asserts a token from the head and a token from the tail both survive
steps: prompt:explain the wrapping rules at length
scenarios.observe: The paragraph soft-wraps across several rows at the terminal width. Head, middle and tail tokens all survive and no ellipsis is inserted. At ~290 characters against a 120-column terminal, head and tail cannot both be present without the line having wrapped onto multiple rows, so this also proves wrapping rather than clipping.

match.userInputContains: explain the wrapping rules at length

events.content: HeadMarker begins a deliberately long single logical line that the renderer has to soft wrap because it is far wider than the terminal, and it passes MidMarker on the way through with filler clauses so the wrap happens several times over before the sentence finally arrives at TailMarker.

scenarios.description: A table renders with borders and padded cells. Pins ASCII mode so the border characters are deterministic, which also exercises the accessibility glyph path
steps: prompt:compare the two languages in a table
scenarios.observe: The table renders as a bordered grid with ASCII box characters, header cells padded to the widest value in each column ('Lang' padded to the width of 'Python'), and the markdown alignment row consumed rather than printed as a data row.

scenarios.name: Markdown table stacks into labelled rows when the terminal is narrow
scenarios.description: The same table content that renders as a grid at full width must fall back to stacked 'Header: value' rows in a narrow terminal, proving the responsive table path
steps: prompt:compare the languages in a narrow view
scenarios.observe: At 48 columns a five-column grid cannot fit, so each row is emitted as labelled 'Header: value' lines with a blank line between rows and no borders at all. ASCII mode is pinned so that a regression back to grid rendering would print '| Lang' and trip the negative assertion -- in Unicode mode the cell separator is a box-drawing bar and that negative would be vacuous.

scenarios.name: Inline link shows its label and destination
scenarios.description: A markdown link renders as a styled label followed by its URL, with the bracket syntax consumed
scenarios.observe: The label renders in the link colour and the destination follows in parentheses, so the URL stays visible in terminals without hyperlink support. Asserting the joined 'label (url)' string pins the order and the parentheses, which independent label and URL checks would not. The bracket-and-paren markdown syntax is consumed. Link colour and any OSC 8 hyperlink escape are not asserted -- neither survives into the screen snapshot.

scenarios.name: Streamed reasoning renders, reassembles and settles once the answer starts
scenarios.description: Two reasoning chunks then the spoken answer -- asserts the chunks concatenate into one block, the header settles from the in-flight 'Thinking...' to 'Thought for', and the reasoning stays separate from the answer
steps: prompt:weigh the two options and answer
verify: screen.contains:ReasonStepOne weighing the options. ReasonStepTwo picking one.
scenarios.observe: The reasoning arrives as two events and renders as ONE body line -- asserting the joined string is what proves the client concatenates chunks rather than emitting a block per event. The header settles to 'Thought for Ns'; the absent 'Thinking...' and 'esc to cancel' are the load-bearing half, because a turn that never ends its thinking phase leaves both on screen after the turn is over, and the reasoning body alone cannot tell the two apart.

scenarios.name: ASCII mode replaces every Unicode glyph on a reasoning turn
scenarios.description: The same reasoning turn under KIRO_ASCII_MODE=1 -- asserts the message bullet, reasoning gutter, summary marker and submit hint all degrade to ASCII and no Unicode form survives
verify: screen.contains:ask a question or describe a task enter
scenarios.observe: Every asserted ASCII form has its Unicode counterpart asserted absent in the same frame, so the pair fails from either side: a regression that stops degrading a glyph fails the notContains, and one that degrades it to the wrong character fails the contains. The four cover distinct call sites -- message bullet, reasoning gutter, turn-summary marker, prompt-bar submit hint -- so a partial degradation is caught rather than averaged away.

scenarios.name: A metered turn reports its usage in the turn summary
scenarios.description: A response carrying a metering event -- asserts the metered amount and its plural unit reach the turn summary line beneath the answer
scenarios.observe: The metered amount renders as 'Tokens: 1234.00' -- pluralised unit, capitalised, two decimal places, which is a formatting decision the bare number would not catch. A turn with no metering event renders the same summary line carrying only 'Time:', so the Tokens segment appearing at all is attributable to the event.

scenarios.name: Streamed context usage reaches the status bar
scenarios.description: A response carrying a context-usage event -- asserts the streamed percentage reaches the status bar rather than the boot placeholder persisting
scenarios.observe: The status bar reads '73%' only because the stream said so -- with no context-usage event the same bar renders the 1% it boots with, so the asserted number cannot appear by default. The percentage is asserted without its adjacent fill glyph, which tracks the value and would couple this to an unrelated presentation choice.
